body: PR 205 closed and superseded by https://github.com/SatanshuMishra/logbook/pull/207 on the same branch, carrying a Supersedes link back. Exactly one open PR on that branch. Title unchanged at "test(close-thread): pin the pointer release order and id-only rule", judged still accurate because all three cases pin the same two rules, and the test: type retained because no control flow moved.U+000AU+000AIts own receipts, run rather than copied from my brief: npm test exit 0 at 821 tests 821 passed 0 failed, typecheck exit 0. The concurrent.distinct-ids race did NOT fire on this run, passing at 4265ms, so no second run was needed.U+000AU+000ATwo judgement calls by that engineer worth keeping, both correct.U+000AU+000AIt declined to re-run the mutation proofs and carried them as not-verified, on the stated reasoning that re-running someone else's proof is a re-verification round rather than a new check. That is the delegation rule applied correctly by a subagent without being told.U+000AU+000AIt DROPPED a not-verified line from the old body reading "a fixture that forces the ledger commit itself to fail - not run", because commit 5a4b0150 added exactly that fixture and it passed in the run above. Carrying it forward would have been a stale and now false claim. Dropping a not-verified line because the gap closed is the right move and the opposite of the usual failure, which is carrying a stale verified line forward.U+000AU+000ABoth PR-body corrections cost a PR number, which is the unavoidable price of a tool with no edit verb. Current open set on this work: 206 for the rendering fix, 207 for the close_thread pins. 204 and 205 are closed and linked from their successors.
